decisions.reason: The October 9 report falls within September 11–October 10 freshness dates, but concerns a police-tip submission rather than customer, competitor, or market research. The quoted police statement supports an attributed incident account; the July event is older, with newly reported discovery and notification. The underlying test methods and promised Anthropic report are absent, so this cannot establish research-tool accuracy or small-business workflow risks beyond a general analogy.

The October 6 organizer-authored guide provides conference logistics and promotes registration, sponsors, and paid recording access. It supplies no substantive research capability, inspectable evaluation, or documented constraint affecting small-business evidence gathering. Its commercial incentives are explicit; descriptions of useful sessions and demos do not establish effectiveness, cost savings, or research reliability.

The October 6 practitioner account connects lightweight classification to sentiment scoring and dataset labeling. Retained passages stating 'I tuned it on my own data' and 'you have to provide the data and context' support an attributed pilot experience and a useful preparation constraint. No sample, benchmark, baseline, timing, or cost measurements support 'much better accuracy,' replacement of frontier models, or orders-of-magnitude savings; decline those conclusions. The author sells training and consulting, and a weekend coding project may exceed readers' technical capacity. Small-business deployments, unsuccessful trials, non-English performance, and handling or consent for customer data are unexamined. Flag possible cross-posting for review: social-style formatting suggests it, but the supplied evidence establishes no duplicate.

The October 9 qualitative account documents practical constraints relevant to maintaining competitor-research context and synthesizing client calls: 'files went stale or missing,' connections expired, and Claude confused who performed work in client communications. These observations support attributed examples and pilot checks for maintenance, provenance, and context boundaries. Participants were daily expert Claude users; sample size, recruitment, geography, study dates, and systematic performance measures are missing, limiting transfer to small businesses and non-English markets. The prediction that less technical users fare worse is an inference, not a measured result. Reported failures provide useful counterevidence, but customer perspectives, disclosure consent, and data handling are absent; recommendations to connect transcripts or let agents edit files do not establish safety or savings. No supplied evidence establishes sponsorship, cross-posting, or a repeated underlying study elsewhere in this batch.
